item.title: Akita Kanto Festival: Balancing 50 kg Lantern Poles — Guide
item.description: One of Tohoku’s four great festivals and a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage — the Akita Kanto Festival fills the city’s main boulevard for four evenings in early August with performers balancing towering bamboo poles hung with up to 46 lit paper lanterns on their palms, foreheads and shoulders. Each pole weighs 50 kg and stands 12 m tall. Daytime training sessions let visitors try a smaller practice pole. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Akita City, Akita Hours Evenings, early August (4 days) Admission Free to watch; paid seats available Time needed 2 hours Best time Early August (fixed dates) Highlights 50 kg, 12 m bamboo poles hung with 46 lanterns.

item.title: Morioka Sansa Odori: The World's Largest Taiko Parade — Guide
item.description: The world’s largest taiko drum parade by Guinness record — Morioka Sansa Odori fills the city centre for four evenings in early August with tens of thousands of dancers and thousands of taiko drummers performing the Sansa dance through the streets. The hypnotic rhythm of the massed drums is audible from kilometres away. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Morioka, Iwate Hours Aug 1–4, evenings Admission Free (paid seats available) Time needed 2–3 hours Best time August 1–4 Highlights A Guinness-record massed taiko drum parade.

item.title: Omagari Fireworks Championship: Japan's Top Pyrotechnics — Guide
item.description: Japan’s most prestigious fireworks competition — held in Daisen (formerly Omagari) on the last Saturday of August, this century-old competition draws 30 pyrotechnic teams from across Japan to display their finest original creations. Over 18,000 shells light up the night sky above the Omono River before some 800,000 spectators, judged for artistry as much as scale. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Daisen, Akita Hours Evening, last Saturday of August Admission Free viewing; paid seats sell out early Time needed 3 hours Best time Last Saturday of August (fixed) Highlights 30 pyrotechnic teams competing nationally.

item.title: Sumiyoshi Matsuri Guide: Osaka's Great Summer Purification Festival
item.description: Held at the end of summer, the Sumiyoshi Matsuri is the grand festival of Sumiyoshi Taisha, one of Osaka’s oldest and most important shrines — and it traditionally closes the city’s festival season each year. Centred on purification and renewal, its highlights are the solemn Nagoshi-no-harae rite, in which participants pass through a great reed ring to cleanse themselves of the year’s impurities, and a boisterous procession that carries a giant mikoshi (portable shrine) across the Yamato River to a related shrine in Sakai.
